Rhea V: heads-up, got a bug report from an enterprise customer: SDK v1.12.0 started sending header X-Route instead of x-route, and our ingress treats them as different keys.
Tom C: wow, header casing? http headers are supposed to be case-insensitive at transport, but some of our internal proxy layers normalize differently.
Kaito: Confirmed in logs: older proxies canonicalize to lower-case; the new edge proxy keeps original case for legacy reasons (fast-path). So we end up with both x-route and X-Route in the event envelope after enrichment.
Rhea V: The consequence: console charts show split traffic and quota counting picks the first-seen header, which flips some tenant billing unexpectedly.
Tom C: Short-term: add ingestion canonicalizer that lowercases all routing header keys and collapses duplicates, annotate event with route_header_canonicalized=true.
Kaito: Agree. I'll craft a tiny fix in telemetry-ingest to normalize header names before expansion. Canary it to telemetry-canary.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: telemetry-ingest-canary scheduled (v0.90)
Rhea V: Devex action: publish migration note to SDK release notes and add a lint rule that warns when header names use mixed-case. We should also publish a breaking-change advisory for major customers.
Tom C: Longer-term: we should enforce a contract in the SDKs to always emit lower-case header names and update client tests. Also update the proxy compatibility tests to assert canonicalization.
Kaito: I'll add unit+e2e tests that simulate mixed-case headers and assert metrics are stable.
Rhea V: Owners: Kaito (ingest + tests), Tom (SDK guidance + lint), Rhea (customer comms). Timeline: canary now, wide ingest rollout in ~4h if green, SDK lint release tomorrow.
Tom C: I'll open a tiny PR in python/ts/go SDKs with the lint and a note in CHANGELOG.
Rhea V: Filing follow-up thread in #billing for reconciliation with finance if spikes persist.
Kaito: PRs: telemetry#412, tests#88.
Rhea V: thanks. closing loop here after canary results.
